FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 21 October 1975. after the draft finalized by the Food Hygiene. Sampling and Analysis Sectional Commi ttee had been approved by the

Agricultural and Food Products Division Council. 0.2 Amino acids are evaluated in a large number of proteinous foods.
There are mainly two methods, namely, chemical and microbiological for amino acid anal)-sis. Of these two methods, the microbiological method amino acid analyser is not available in most the laboratories owing to its high cost. However. with a view to avoiding interlaboratory differences in microbiological method which rna y affect the ultimate results, this standard has been formulated. It is expected that this method will help in achieving uniformity in methods of analysis of amino acids thereby facilitating interpretation and comparison of results. 0.3 In reporting the results of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS: 2�1960',

is simpler, less cumbenome and offen reproducible result~ especially when

or

1. SCOPE
1.1 This standard prescribes a microbiological method for estimation of essential amino acids in food.

2. PRINCIPLE
2.1 The method is based on the observation that certain micro-organisms

require specific nutrients ror growth. Usilll a basal medium complete in aU respects except for the amino acid under test� growth responses of the organisms are compared quantitatively in standard and in unkno\vn IOlutions. Either the acid or the turbidity produced by the organisms i. meuured to determine the alent or growtb and thereby the amount or
nutrient in the test IOlution.

6.PROCEDURB
6.1 Stuard Tab�� - Sterilize the tubes of basal medium containing standard levels of amino acid as in 5.11 by autoclaving at 120�C for 10 minutes. Cool to room temperature and inoculate 3 tubes of each standard with the inoculum as in 4.5. For acidimetric titration method (s" 6.3 ), incubate the inoculated tubes at 37�C for 72 hours, except for cystine where it should be done for 18 to 24 hours. If turbidimetric method (s" G.t) is used, incubate the inoculated tubes at 37�0 for )6 to

20 hours,
6.2 Sample Tab.. - Sterilize the tubes of samples ( 5.13 ) as in 6.1.

.

6.3 Aeicllmetrlc Method 6.3.1 Standard SDluliofi - 0-02 N sodium hydroxide and 0-1 percent bromothymol blue indicator solution. 6.3.2 Transfer the contents quantitatively to a J50�ml conical flask, rinsing the tubes with distilled water twice. Add about 0-2 ml or 0�) percent bromothymol blue indicator and titrate the solution against 0�02 H sodium hydroxide to an end point of greenish blue colour around pH 6-8. A pH meter may be used in place of the indicator solution. 6.33 CaJeul.'ion - Draw a standard curve for the assay by plotting the volume of 0�02 H sodium hydroxide on the r-axis agaimt concentration of the amino acid per tube in the standard series on the X-axis. It is
preferable to plot these on logarithmic scale in order to obtain a straight line or a type of curve where the Itraight line of the curve can be utilized to determine amino acid content in the sample tubes. Determine amino acid content of tubes in the unknown series by interpolation of the titre values on the standard curve. Calculate the average for I ml of test solutionfrom values obtained from not len than three tubes which do not vary by more than 10 percent of the average. Calculate the amino acid

content of the test solution using the following relationship: Avera.c "1 perml X volume X �.. t ami �dl 1 diluting factor III or ~ DO &CI IIaIDP e Mass of the sample
